points.statement: Introduces an open-source simulator designed to enable embodied agents to perform collaborative tasks by leveraging Theory of Mind.
points.quote: This paper introduces an open-source simulator, BeliefNest, designed to enable embodied agents to perform collaborative tasks by leveraging Theory of Mind.

points.statement: Dynamically and hierarchically constructs simulators within a Minecraft environment, letting agents explicitly represent nested belief states about themselves and others.
points.quote: BeliefNest dynamically and hierarchically constructs simulators within a Minecraft environment, allowing agents to explicitly represent nested belief states about themselves and others.

points.statement: The simulator provides a prompt generation mechanism based on each belief state, facilitating design and evaluation of methods for agent control utilizing LLMs.
points.quote: The simulator provides a prompt generation mechanism based on each belief state, facilitating the design and evaluation of methods for agent control utilizing large language models (LLMs).

points.statement: Each agent can perform mental simulations within its own simulator, considering the beliefs of others, to generate action plans reflecting those beliefs.
points.quote: Each agent can perform mental simulations within its own simulator, considering the beliefs of others, to generate action plans that reflect these beliefs.

points.statement: Proposes an open-source simulator designed to support research on collaborative behavior in embodied agents endowed with Theory of Mind capabilities.
points.quote: In this paper, we propose BeliefNest, an open-source simulator designed to support research on collaborative behavior in embodied agents endowed with Theory of Mind capabilities.
